To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cyclosporin A (CsA), a potent immunosuppressive agent, causes oxidative damage in rabbit hepatic tissue and that antioxidant vitamin supplementation can prevent this damage.
CsA induces oxidant stress and, peroxidation in hepatic tissues, which may be responsible from the CsA-induced toxicity.
CsA impairs the antioxidant enzyme activities in the liver and thus, leads peroxidative damage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possible molecular mechanisms leading to CsA-induced hepatopathy.
the possible role of oxidative stress in the CsA induced hepatotoxicity and the protective effect of antioxidant vitamin supplementation in this respect.
the possible molecular mechanisms underlying cyclosporine hepatotoxicity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cyclosporin A is a hepatotoxin, which causes oxidant stress in rabbit hepatic cells, and antioxidant vitamins may be effective against this toxic effect.
cyclosporin-induced hepatotoxicity can be attributed to the oxidant-antioxidant imbalance and the antioxidant vitamins may prevent this imbalance and, thus, the CsA-induced toxicity.
CsA causes hepatotoxicity by inducing oxidant stress, which can be inhibited by vitamin administration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cyclosporin A induced oxidative stress in rabbit hepatic tissue and that the oxidative stress can be prevented by vitamin supplementation.
the CsA-induced oxidative injury can be prevented by the combined use of antioxidant vitamins.
cyclosporin-induced hepatic tissue damages can be prevented by vitamin E and C supplementation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CsA-induced oxidative stress can be prevented by vitamin therapy.
the antioxidant defense systems of the liver are impaired in the presence of CsA and the antioxidant vitamin supplementation is a useful strategy to prevent CsA-induced hepatocyte damage.
